author: Brian Soule
title: Well I have been waiting for a pullback for a number of stoc
text:
Well I have been waiting for a pullback for a number of stocks, and Apple Inc ( AAPL ) was one of the stocks I had been waiting for. In one of my very first articles that I wrote last May I was looking for a potential replacement for International Business Machines Corp ( IBM ) in my portfolio, having come to the conclusion that I no longer wanted to be invested in IBM. In that article AAPL was compared to several other tech giants, with the winner being Cisco Systems Inc ( CSCO ) which has been part of the Sand in Shoes portfolio since last August. However, AAPL came in a very close second and I have always wanted an excuse, er, reason to own some shares of AAPL. This most recent downturn was my opportunity.
So why Apple? I am not a "techie" that camps out for the newest phone or tablet or even understands much about them but I can't imagine life without my iPhone. I don't own even close to the latest model, but I love having the one I have and I believe I'm on my fourth one since I gave up the old flip phone and moved into the world of smart phones. In our small Soule household we have, not counting defunct devices sitting in a drawer somewhere, five Apple devices for three people.
But to get more specific, another reason I want to own AAPL is due to their tremendous financial statements. All three of them (income statement, balance sheet, statement of cash flows) read like a dream. They have ever increasing revenues, they have cash coming out of their ears, they are generating free cash flow like very few companies can, and they are buying back shares and increasing their dividend.
As I said, they came in a very close second to CSCO when I reviewed both companies about 8 months ago. Since that time, my metrics have changed slightly and AAPL has finished off another fiscal year, so I ran the numbers through all of my guidelines to make sure I did still want to own the stock. So let's get started.
